transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Nguyen (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (CascadeEdge Head of ML), Tomás Rivera (CascadeEdge Director of Platform), Janice Li (CascadeEdge FinOps), Evan Cole (CascadeEdge SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
Redwood walked through the Console route economics pages focused on per-route usage & cost attribution. Demo covered token-level cost breakdowns, route filters, prefix caching impact, batching recommendations from Optimize, and routing policies for dedicated vs hosted instances. Customer asked about encryption/KMS, SOC2, and how to attribute shared models across teams. Next step: pricing worksheet + POC scope.

[00:00] Lena Park: All right hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Lena from Redwood, and with me is Marcus on the SE side. Quick roll call?

[00:06] Priya Shah: Hi this is Priya, hi Tomás, Janice here as well. We're excited to see the console end-to-end.

[00:12] Lena Park: Great, thanks. We'll keep this to about 45 minutes of demo, 10 minutes of Q&A, happy to go deeper afterwards. High level we'll show per-route dashboards, the cost breakdown, and then Marcus will jump into the Optimize suggestions and how caching/batching change the numbers. We'll also address security questions at the end.

[00:28] Tomás Rivera: Sounds good. Our main ask is: we need a clear way to attribute spend across our product routes — search, summarization, and in-app suggestions — and show FinOps why numbers spiked two weeks ago.

[00:40] Marcus Nguyen: Totally. We'll start in the Console, I'll share my screen now. 

[00:46] [screen share noise] 

[01:05] Marcus Nguyen: Here is the Routes view — you'll see a list of routes (we auto-group by path or tag). In your account we can map the routes to product teams. The default columns show calls, tokens in, tokens out, average latency, and estimated cost. Note the cost is a derived metric using model unit pricing plus a fudge for batching/caching where applicable.

[01:33] Janice Li: That 'estimated cost' — is that per-token cost including infra? We're only allowed to show our own cost lines in FinOps.

[01:41] Lena Park: Good question. Right now the estimated cost is per-token inference cost (model + GPU amortized), plus an optional line for networking. If you purchase Dedicated or Private we can show committed cost vs overage. We can also export per-route CSV for your internal chargeback.

[01:58] Priya Shah: Can it break down embeddings vs generation? Our embedding calls are cheap but very chatty.

[02:05] Marcus Nguyen: Yes, we tag by API endpoint and model type. See the filter here: Embedding endpoints vs Completion/Chat. You can pivot out embeddings.

[02:18] [short pause] Speaker 1: mm-hmm

[02:22] Marcus Nguyen: I'm going to drill into the Summarization route. On the right pane there's a token waterfall that shows token input vs output and cost attribution by model version. Important to note: if you do model fallbacks (e.g., gen-1 -> gen-2 cheaper), the cost column will show weighted average by traffic split.

[02:45] Tomás Rivera: We also have a canary where 20% goes to a quantized variant — does that show separately?

[02:51] Marcus Nguyen: Yep, it will appear as a sub-route under the same route name (we annotate as variant: v2-quant). You can toggle grouping to see combined or broken-out.

[03:05] Marcus Nguyen: Now switching to the Cost Explorer: here's the timeline for the past 30 days. You can hover to see attribution: routes, models, and regions. The spike two weeks ago — looks like a short-lived increase in tokens for the 'suggestions' route, probably a looped client issue — you can click the point to open top user agents and top prompts snippet (we obfuscated by default).

[03:36] Evan Cole: Are the top prompts stored? We cannot store PII; what data retention controls do we have?

[03:42] Lena Park: By default we retain metadata and aggregates. Full request logs are optional and can be configured to redact or not persist prompt text. For Private we support customer-controlled retention and gateway side redaction. We also have KMS integration for envelope encryption — see our security pack link.

[03:58] Marcus Nguyen: Quick demo of Optimize suggestions — this is where we recommend batching window sizes and suggest quantized model variants based on your latency SLO. For 'suggestions' route, the optimizer suggests set max_batch to 8 and enable prefix caching for repeated prompts. Applying these changes in the Console simulates the expected cost delta — we can preview: estimated -34% token-cost due to KV caching and 10% latency decrease.

[04:30] Priya Shah: That percent looks high. How do you compute it? I want to understand the assumptions.

[04:36] Marcus Nguyen: It's based on observed sequence length distribution and hit-rate estimation for KV cache. We run a quick simulation over the sample traffic (or your uploaded sample) — assumptions are shown in the modal: average seq in/out, cache hit rate estimate, and batching efficiency. You can tweak those numbers if you know your clients have more variance.

[04:57] [background typing]

[05:02] Janice Li: For accounting, we need the exact math to plug into our model. Can you export the baseline and post-Optimize CSV?

[05:08] Lena Park: Yes exportable. We'll include the export in the POC pack.

[05:14] Tomás Rivera: Is there automated tagging? Our routes are thousands, we need to map them to teams and owners.

[05:21] Marcus Nguyen: We support auto-suggested tags using path heuristics and header-based detection, plus a claims-based mapping when you use SSO. We can also ingest your mapping CSV.

[05:33] [07:00ish - transcription drift noise]

[05:38] Marcus Nguyen: On the left is a rules engine for routing. You can set a policy: all production low-latency routes go to Dedicated pool A, burst to Hosted if Dedicated saturated, fallback to smaller cheaper model if latency not critical. These are first-class and can be scheduled for canaries.

[05:58] Priya Shah: For Dedicated, will we still get transparent per-route costs? Our CFO wants committed vs incremental line items.

[06:06] Lena Park: Yes for Dedicated we show committed allocation consumption and remaining commit. Overage shows at per-token rate separate line. We can attach internal chargeback tags so your CFO can break out committed amortized cost vs overage.

[06:17] Priya Shah: What about deployments in region EU / APAC for data residency?

[06:21] Marcus Nguyen: You can filter by region and also route policy can pin a route to region. For Private we can deploy in a customer VPC in region X; that will appear in the console as a region-labeled pool.

[06:34] [small cross talk]

[06:39] Tomás Rivera: Security quick question — we need SOC2 type II evidence and key management.

[06:44] Lena Park: We'll share SOC2 report and our KMS integration doc after the meeting. For Private we also support HSM via your vendor. Link: https://redwood.app/security/soc2.pdf and KMS guide: https://redwood.app/docs/kms-integration.

[07:00] Janice Li: For FinOps, what granularity is the CSV export? We need per-route, per-day, per-model token counts with cost columns.

[07:09] Marcus Nguyen: Yes that's supported. We also provide a pre-baked BigQuery export if you'd like streaming into your data warehouse for internal dashboards.

[07:18] [screen flicker, brief pause]

[07:25] Marcus Nguyen: Quick demo of a Cost Drill: selecting the 'suggestions' route and toggling 'include optimize effects' shows a before/after chart. You can also simulate a canary by changing traffic split — the console recalculates expected spend.

[07:43] Priya Shah: If we enable prefix caching, what are the privacy implications? Do cached prefixes ever get shared across customers?

[07:51] Lena Park: No sharing across customers. Cache is namespace-scoped to your account or to a pool depending on config. For Private you control the cache lifecycle entirely.

[07:59] Evan Cole: Any additional network egress costs shown? We have large embedding exports that cause storage+egress fees.

[08:06] Marcus Nguyen: We surface network egress as an optional line item — by default it's not modeled unless you turn it on. We can tie egress to your cloud provider rates if you give us the tariff.

[08:18] [10:00ish - filler speech from attendees confirming]

[08:23] Marcus Nguyen: I'll show the Alerts and Regression monitoring: you can set a quality eval set per route; if the Optimize change causes a >5% quality regression on the eval suite we trigger rollback. That integration is critical for teams who trade cost vs quality.

[08:40] Priya Shah: That's important for us — pleased to see eval hooks.

[08:46] Tomás Rivera: Onboarding: how fast can we get a POC? We have compliance gating so need Private for the POC.

[08:54] Lena Park: Typical Private POC is 2-4 weeks to spin up a customer VPC deployment if there is capacity; we'll include a scoped runbook. I'll loop in the infra team. Marcus can run the initial benchmarks on your sample traffic.

[09:08] Janice Li: Pricing question: do you have a committed reserved capacity discount ladder?

[09:13] Lena Park: Yes reserved capacity for Dedicated uses a commit-based contract; scale discounts apply by GPU-hour commit. We'll put the exact tiers in the worksheet we send.

[09:23] [brief pause, technical noise]

[09:28] Marcus Nguyen: Last bit — API and SDKs: the per-request metadata we add (route, team-tag) can be added via headers, and we have middleware for common frameworks. We'll share the mapping examples.

[09:40] Priya Shah: Ok thanks. Can you also show how to backfill route tags historically?

[09:46] Marcus Nguyen: You can run the backfill job from the Console: upload a CSV mapping and the job will apply tags to historical logs. It takes a bit but is straightforward.

[09:58] Lena Park: Let's do quick recap and next steps.

[10:02] Lena Park: Recap: 1) Console shows per-route token-level attribution, embeddings vs generation split, and committed vs overage lines for Dedicated. 2) Optimize suggests batching/quantization/prefix caching with simulated cost deltas. 3) Security: SOC2, KMS and Private options available. 4) Next: we'll send pricing worksheet and security pack, Marcus will start initial cost projections based on your 7-day sample.

[10:28] Tomás Rivera: Perfect. Tomás will share logs and Priya will confirm our eval suite.

[10:35] Priya Shah: Yep we'll upload the sample.

[10:38] Lena Park: Great. I'll follow up with the POC runbook and the meeting notes. Links referenced: deck: https://redwood.app/links/cascadeedge-demo-deck , security pack: https://redwood.app/security/soc2.pdf , sample benchmark sheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/cascadeedge-sample.xlsx

[10:56] Janice Li: Thanks everyone.

[11:00] Meeting end (approx).

Notes on transcript: occasional speaker mislabels and auto-transcription errors present. There were a few quick technical digressions from Marcus about kernel selection and KV cache hit estimation where phrases were partially garbled by the auto-transcriber (e.g., "KV cash" or "kernel sel"), and some timestamps drift (~07:00 references above are approximate).
